newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fischler pledges to defend EU farmers in WTO talks.
newsitem.headline: Fischler pledges to defend EU farmers in WTO talks.

text.p: The European Union will fully respect its international commitments in the next round of world trade negotiations but must defend its farmers' interests, EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Monday.

Fischler said in a speech in Tokyo that certain trading partners were already seeking the abolition of some EU direct income support payments to farmers, further reductions in farm subsidies and increased market access.

"While they have every right to mark out their negotiating position, we equally have every right to reject demands which would serve to undermine our interests," Fischler said in a speech, a copy of which was released in Brussels.
Free trade is not an answer to all our problems, he said, looking ahead to the next round of World Trade Organisation (WTO) farm trade negotiations due to start in 1999
"Our aim is to ensure a decent livelihood for all farmers in Europe...This is our social responsibility and it will not be solved by market forces alone," he said.
This was a natural aim for the EU, the world's largest food importer, and Japanese agricultural policy seemed to have the same objective, he added.
Environmental and social objectives must also be considered as well as trade liberalisation.
"European agriculture and the rural landscape...will not be sacrificed on the altar of unfettered free trade," he said.
Japan and the EU should work together to strengthen international demand for sustainable agriculture and rural development, he added.
